items.title: Combining phosphorus sources with different reactivities
items.text: The authors use rapidly reacting P(SiMe3)3 with slower P(SiPh3)3 to help separate nucleation from subsequent growth. They interpret the slower precursor as a reservoir that can continue supplying growth material. This is a mechanistic interpretation supported by their comparisons, not a direct measurement of instantaneous monomer concentration.

items.title: Why nucleation control alone is insufficient
items.text: The authors conclude that separating nucleation and growth in time does not by itself ensure a narrow size distribution in covalent InP. Monomer consumption during growth also matters. Their optical, TEM and simplified spherical-model comparisons support this interpretation; the model outputs remain calculated quantities.
